bullets.title: INTC: Massive 2Q beat; raises capex to $20B+; stocks fades post-call
bullets.body: Intel reported 2Q26 revenue of $16.13B (+25% YoY vs. $14.4B consensus) and EPS of $0.42 vs. $0.22 est, driven by DCAI revenue of $6.26B (+59.9% YoY). 3Q guidance of $15.8-$16.8B and $0.38 EPS well above consensus. FY26 capex raised from $17B to $20B+ with FY27 guided 'significantly higher.' 18A yields ahead of targets, 14A targeting 2028 HVM. However, stock faded post-call—investors frustrated by equity raise disclosure, 14A described as 'internal products only,' and capex guidance spread across all segments vs. foundry-focused. Sell-side consensus: PT range $109-$155, avg ~$116. KeyBanc raised to $155 OW; Roth to $120 Buy; UBS Neutral at $121; Wolfe Peer Perform.

bullets.title: AMD: AI Day lifts PT to $650-$730; Helios in production, Anthropic 2GW win, TAM to $1.4T
bullets.body: AMD's Advancing AI Day 2026 delivered outsized positive signals: Helios rack-scale GPU platform in full production with shipments starting Sept 2026; Anthropic committed to 2GW of MI450/MI455X (1GW deploying 1H27); extended Microsoft Azure partnership; OpenAI and Meta each deploying 6GW. AI accelerator TAM raised to $1.4T by 2030 (45%+ CAGR) and server CPU TAM to $220B (50%+ CAGR). Multiple houses raised PTs: UBS $700→$730, Roth $500→$650, Wolfe $650 OW. AMD Venice CPU achieves 2.8x agents-per-watt vs. NVIDIA Vera. AMD-Cerebras disaggregated inference delivers 5x tokens-per-second-per-watt advantage.

bullets.title: CHTR: 2Q EBITDA miss, broadband ARPU declining; analysts expect guidance cuts
bullets.body: Charter reported 2Q26 revenue of $13.53B (slight beat) but adj. EBITDA of $5.45B missed the $5.58B consensus by 200+ bps, with margins down 110bps YoY to 40.3%. Core residential HSD net losses accelerated to -166K/-212K depending on source; broadband ARPU fell 1.5% YoY. Mobile lines +406K beat expectations (+18.9% YoY revenue). FCF of $969M missed. UBS maintains Neutral. KeyBanc expects company to talk down EBITDA, internet net add, and ARPU guidance. Stock down ~5.7% premarket.

bullets.title: VZ: 2Q beat on FCF and postpaid phone adds; raises FY26 guidance
bullets.body: Verizon reported 2Q26 adj. EPS of $1.30 (beat $1.28E) and FCF of $6.43B (well above $5.28B est), though revenue of $34.25B missed $35.16B consensus. Postpaid phone net adds of +184K crushed +112K consensus; postpaid ARPA fell 1.4% YoY. Raised FY26 mobility/broadband service revenue guidance to 2.5-3.0%, EPS to $4.99-5.04 (6-7% growth), and FCF to $21.9-22.1B. UBS and KeyBanc both maintain Neutral/Sector Weight.

bullets.title: DLR: Record 2Q bookings and backlog; Citi upgrades to Buy, JPM raises PT to $235
bullets.body: Digital Realty reported record 0-1MW plus interconnection bookings of $108M in 2Q26 (third consecutive record quarter), with total backlog rising to $1.4B DLR share ($1.9B at 100%). Two additional hyperscale leases signed in July totaling $205M DLR share. FY26 guidance raised: revenue +$200M, EBITDA +$100M, core FFO/sh +$0.13. Management projects double-digit core FFOPS growth through at least 2028. UBS raises PT to $227 (Buy); JPMorgan raises PT to $235; Citi upgrades to Buy citing AI-driven demand tailwind.

bullets.title: ORCL and CRM win massive government contracts; ORCL +2.2% premarket
bullets.body: Oracle was awarded a $3.31B US Navy five-year software contract and a separate $7B 10-year Pentagon software consolidation deal. Salesforce won a $1.6B three-year VA contract. ORCL trading +2.2% in premarket; CRM +1.7%.

bullets.title: TSLA: Down 14.5% on worst day since March 2025; management cautious on autonomy scaling
bullets.body: Tesla shares fell 14.5% Thursday, worst single day since March 2025, after management cautioned against scaling unsupervised autonomy until ~40 test vehicles demonstrate safety—providing no specifics on paid rides or active autonomous vehicles. Short sellers banked ~$4.1-4.3B in mark-to-market gains. Waymo comparison: 3,500 unsupervised AVs and 500K paid rides/week vs. Tesla's ~40 vehicles and ~4K rides/week.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Down 7.1%, breaks 200-day MA; capex raise and token growth deceleration concern investors
bullets.body: Alphabet fell 7.1% Thursday—its worst day in years—after raising FY26 capex guidance by $15B to $195-205B, raising AI spending sustainability concerns. Token growth decelerated to 38% QoQ vs. 60% prior quarter. GOOGL broke below its 200-day moving average for the first time in over a year, and is down 13%+ on the week. Market cap loss ~$300B. Cloud growth was +82% YoY but elevated capex weighed on sentiment. Hedge funds had added tactical shorts ahead of earnings.

bullets.title: DELL and HPE: Citi raises PTs to $515/$74 on larger CPU TAM and AI server demand
bullets.body: Citi raised Dell Technologies PT from $475 to $515 and HPE PT from $70 to $74, citing Intel's +60% YoY DC growth, AMD's server CPU TAM expansion to $220B by 2030, and strengthening enterprise AI infrastructure demand. Both maintained at Buy with upside catalyst watches through Oct 22. PC vendors with larger volume (Apple, Dell) seen better positioned to gain share as PC units decline low-double digits in FY26 on memory constraints.

bullets.title: Mag 7 loses $797B in single day; biggest collective drop since April 2025
bullets.body: All seven Mag 7 names fell more than 1% Thursday, with the basket down 4.8%—the largest one-day selloff in five years—erasing $797B in combined market value. TSLA (-14.5%) and GOOGL (-7.1%) were the primary drivers. AI capex ROI uncertainty, rising oil above $100/bbl, higher rates (10Y above 4.7%), and new 10-12.5% tariffs on 60+ countries all contributed. Mag 7 bouncing modestly Friday with S&P futures +0.2%.

bullets.title: NVDA: $1.5B Amkor partnership for US chip packaging; GPU residual value guarantees enable bank financing
bullets.body: Nvidia signed a multi-year strategic partnership with Amkor Technology including $1.5B prepayment to expand US advanced packaging and test capacity. Separately, NVIDIA reportedly implementing GPU residual value guarantees (price floors) to enable bank financing of AI clusters. 800V HVDC architecture targeting production in 1Q27 with Delta Electronics positioned for 2Q ramp.

bullets.title: TMUS: Down >10% on beat-and-reiterate; MS reiterates OW at $230, Wolfe cuts PT to $236
bullets.body: T-Mobile fell over 10% despite reporting 2Q26 results above estimates—postpaid phone net adds of +277K, service revenue +9% YoY, core adj. EBITDA +12%—and raising FY26 FCF guidance by $200M. Management guided 3Q KPIs below consensus citing rate plan modernization churn friction. Morgan Stanley reiterates Top Pick Overweight at $230, calling stock at 7x EV/EBITDA its lowest multiple in 5+ years. Wolfe cuts PT to $236 from previous but keeps Outperform.

bullets.title: UBER: Piper most bullish in gig economy; institutional interest high (Ackman 15.7%, Tepper tripled stake)
bullets.body: Piper Sandler is most bullish on UBER among gig economy and OTA cohort. Citi previews 2Q26 earnings (Aug 5), projecting total gross bookings of $57.3B (+20% YoY ex-FX) and adj. EBITDA of $2.78B. Separately, David Tepper nearly tripled UBER stake to ~6.3M shares and Bill Ackman holds 15.7% of his portfolio in UBER.

bullets.title: MSFT: KeyBanc reiterates OW at $600 PT but flags FY27 capex upside risk
bullets.body: KeyBanc estimates MSFT FY27 capex ~$17B above consensus and warns the figure may still be too low. GOOGL's negative stock reaction to elevated capex makes KeyBanc more concerned MSFT cloud upside must be substantial to offset capex pressure. Azure bulls target mid-40s% growth. Key risks: OpenAI dependence, non-AI Azure slowdown, and slower Copilot adoption.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Morgan Stanley cuts PT to $29; broadband competition intensifies from FWA/Starlink/fiber
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley lowered CMCSA PT from $30 to $29 and maintains Equal-weight, projecting 2027-28 as increasingly painful as DSL migration wanes while fiber, FWA, and Starlink expand. 2Q26 residential broadband net losses -167K; ARPU down 3.8% YoY. Peacock achieved profitability for first time with +$189M EBITDA. Wolfe recommends CMCSA/CHTR pair trade with CMCSA preferred on lower leverage.

bullets.title: META: $12B Texas data center financing at 7% yields, 40bps higher than prior Hyperion deal
bullets.body: Meta faces rising borrowing costs, securing $12B Texas data center financing at 7% yields—40bps higher than the $27B Hyperion deal nine months ago. Meta launched a new Seller app for Facebook Marketplace with AI-powered listing tools for US merchants.

bullets.title: RDDT: Sentiment decisively positive ahead of 2Q; analyst expects $775M revenue vs. $730M Street
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects Reddit to beat 2Q revenue by $50-60M above the high end of guidance (~$775M vs. $730M Street). Q3 adj. EBITDA margin expected ~44% with guide of $360-370M. Investor sentiment shifted to decisively positive. Citi previews strong digital ad environment with rising engagement metrics supporting RDDT, PINS, SNAP heading into print.

bullets.title: FSLR: Oversold technicals; 232 tariff policy in August is the binary catalyst
bullets.body: FSLR technicals are oversold (RSI 31) after failing to hold $300 in June; current support at $200-190. Bulls model $350-400 PT if Section 232 lands with ~38c/W MIP and 25-35% AVT; bears risk $160 test if 232 is delayed or diluted. Q2 bookings expected light at ~1.3GW; 50GW/$14B backlog provides revenue visibility through 2028+.

bullets.title: TEAM: Citi reiterates Buy at $110 as down 50% YTD; FY27 guide likely conservative
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy on Atlassian (earnings Aug 6) noting shares are down 50%+ YTD with unjustifiably bearish sentiment. Post-conference intra-Q checks show resilient fundamentals, no material churn. FY27 revenue guidance likely to miss consensus, driven by conservative new CFO and smaller Cloud price increases, but analyst expects beat-and-raise motion through the year. OPCO also sees FY27 guide at/slightly below consensus as likely bottom.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Merger pause extended to Aug 17; judge orders timeline for preliminary injunction
bullets.body: The PSKY-WBD $110B merger pause was extended through August 17 amid legal challenges from US states and screenwriters. Separately, the presiding judge asked both sides to agree on a preliminary injunction hearing timeline and format by July 24 noon, with consequences if parties cannot agree.
